routes.clarification: Do you mean light in vacuum in SI units? The reviewed C010/v2 record covers the definitional value 299,792,458 metres per second in vacuum. Ask: Is the speed of light in vacuum exactly 299,792,458 metres per second? Media and empirical measurement results are outside this record.

questions: Has anyone seen the Great Wall of China from low Earth orbit with the naked eye?
Do the reviewed sources establish that an astronaut has seen the Great Wall of China from low Earth orbit with the unaided eye?
Can you see the Great Wall of China from space?
Is the Great Wall of China visible from space?
routes.clarification: From where, and do you mean an unaided sighting, a photograph, ease of seeing it, or an attributed report? C009/v2 assesses whether its reviewed source package establishes a verified unaided-eye sighting from low Earth orbit; it currently abstains and does not settle whether a sighting occurred. For that evidence assessment, ask: Do the reviewed sources establish that an astronaut has seen the Great Wall of China from low Earth orbit with the unaided eye? Other locations and predicates require separate review.

questions: Is Venus's sidereal axial rotation retrograde?
Is Venus’s sidereal rotation retrograde?
Does Venus rotate retrograde relative to the fixed stars?
Does Venus rotate backwards?
Does Venus rotate clockwise?
routes.clarification: Specify the reference/viewpoint and whether you mean the solid planet, atmosphere or orbit. C011 covers solid-body sidereal axial retrograde rotation in the cited source convention; it does not settle an unspecified clockwise viewpoint, atmosphere, orbital motion or exact period.
